sources.evidence: Silicon is approximately 100 W/(m K), while typical TIM is below 10 W/(m K); the V6 TIM range remains within the previously used 1.33-7.5 W/(m K) model bracket.

sources.title: Compact Thermal Modelling Tool for Fast Design Space Exploration of 3D ICs with Integrated Microchannels
sources.evidence: Uses silicon k=130 and copper spreader k=400 W/(m K), and explicitly models a weak secondary package path.

sources.title: 3D-ICE 4.0: Accurate and efficient thermal modeling for 2.5D/3D heterogeneous chiplet systems
sources.evidence: Preserves material heterogeneity and anisotropy and uses adaptive vertical partitioning for heterogeneous package stacks.
sources.use: method support for explicit anisotropic per-layer fields; not a numeric conductivity source

sampling_interpretation.log_uniform: used for positive quantities spanning a multiplicative range, including TIM, local k, and Robin h
sampling_interpretation.correlated_axes: one Sobol latent drives kxy and kz together for effective anisotropic layers, preserving the reference ordering instead of independently scrambling axes
sampling_interpretation.continuous_power: package power is sampled continuously and independently of boundary-condition family; q follows exactly from power fractions and resolved source volume
not_claimed: Every point inside an engineering envelope is a measured material value
A uniform Robin coefficient represents all package cooling hardware
